message.loconautics_fixes.need_relocator: You need a train relocator in hand.
message.loconautics_fixes.not_owner: This train belongs to someone else.
loconautics_fixes.ponder.transmission.te: The Transmission passes rotation through at a speed set by Redstone
Without a signal the output stays still
A signal on this side sets the output speed: full strength gives 256 RPM, whatever the input speed is
A signal on the opposite side reverses the output
Sneak Click it to set Redstone Link frequencies for speed and direction, so it can be controlled wirelessly
Sneak Click an Analog Controller with the Transmission item to copy the controller's frequencies onto it
loconautics_fixes.ponder.analog_controll: Driving a Train with the Analog Controller
The Analog Controller is the driver's control stand of a physics train
Right Click it to take control, and again to let go
While you control it, throttle and steering are sent over Redstone Link frequencies
Sneak Click it to choose those frequencies
...and Bearing Axles listen to the steering
Sneak Click the controller with either of their items to copy the matching frequencies onto it
Dye can be used to change its color
loconautics_fixes.ponder.bearing_axle.he: Driving a Carriage with a Bearing Axle
loconautics_fixes.ponder.bearing_axle.te: The Bearing Axle is the driving wheel of a carriage
Place it beside a bogey or on top of one
Rotation from the back of the axle drives the train along the rails
Only one Bearing Axle can drive each carriage
It steers using Left and Right signals: Redstone on its sides, or Redstone Link frequencies
Engineer's Goggles show whether it is set up correctly, its gear and the load
loconautics_fixes.ponder.handbrake.heade: Parking a Carriage with the Handbrake
loconautics_fixes.ponder.handbrake.text_: The Handbrake is a parking brake for a single carriage
While powered by Redstone it locks the carriage to the rail, so it can't be driven or roll down a slope
Without a signal the carriage is free again
loconautics_fixes.ponder.knuckle.text_1: Knuckles are automatic couplers for train carriages
loconautics_fixes.ponder.knuckle.text_2: When two Knuckles meet they lock together on a pivot, so the cars hold as one train and still take corners
loconautics_fixes.ponder.knuckle.text_3: Right Click with a Wrench to uncouple them
loconautics_fixes.ponder.knuckle.text_4: On a Knuckle that is not coupled, the Wrench rotates it instead
loconautics_fixes.ponder.knuckle.text_5: Like Copycat blocks, it takes the look of a block you click it with
loconautics_fixes.ponder.screw_link.head: Coupling Carriages with Screw Links
loconautics_fixes.ponder.screw_link.text: Screw Link Headstocks couple carriages with a hanging link and hook
Grab the hook at the end of one link and hang it on the facing headstock to couple them
Right Click a coupled headstock with an empty hand to uncouple
loconautics_fixes.ponder.copycat_headsto: The Copycat Headstock is an end beam for carriages
Like Copycat blocks, it takes the look of a block you click it with
Clicking with the same block again switches between its variants
loconautics_fixes.ponder.turntable.heade: Turning Trains with a Turntable Bearing
loconautics_fixes.ponder.turntable.text_: The Turntable Bearing turns the platform in front of it by an exact angle, then holds it there
Right Click it with an empty hand to turn the blocks in front of it into a turning platform
A Redstone signal starts its next turn
Sneak Click it with an empty hand to edit its instructions: turn by an angle, wait, wait for Redstone, or follow a train schedule
Sneak Click it with a Train Signal to bind the signal: it then stays red while the platform is turned away or holds a train
A train longer than the platform can't be turned
loconautics_fixes.ponder.industrial_pipe: Industrial Pipes, Glass Pipes, Smart Pipes and Valves work the same way as Create's own
The Industrial Pump is powered like a Mechanical Pump...
loconautics_fixes.ponder.industrial_tank: Industrial Fluid Tanks hold 12,000mb per block
A tank lays along the face you click, so it can stand up or lie down
Every touching tank joins into one, in any shape up to 5 blocks wide
Placing a tank on the end of another places a whole layer at once. Sneak to place a single block
Right Click with a Wrench to switch the windows of the whole tank
A Hose Connector goes on the side of a tank
Hoses strung between connectors carry fluid from one carriage's tank to another
Right Click it with a Wrench to remove its newest hose. With no hoses left, the Wrench breaks the connector off
loconautics_fixes.ponder.nozzle_socket.h: Docking Nozzles in a Nozzle Socket
loconautics_fixes.ponder.nozzle_socket.t: The Nozzle Socket is a port on a tank where a Hose Nozzle can dock
Right Click it to open or close its lid
The lid stays open while a nozzle is docked
